title: Electric Service Agreement Reliability Credit Terms: Outage Duration Measured to the Meter Interval
content:
These reliability credit terms of the **Electric Service Agreement** state how Lakeshore Power & Light Company measures the qualifying duration of an outage record for the sustained-outage credit. The measure turns on the interval length of the meter in service at the premise, as the customer's **Metering Service** records show it: the meter in service and the interval length of its meter type.

**Terms.**

(a) Where the meter in service at the premise records interval data in 60-minute intervals, the qualifying duration is the recorded duration rounded up to the next whole hour, because the meter's restoration message only marks the hour.

(b) Where it records 15-minute intervals, the qualifying duration is the recorded duration rounded up to the next quarter hour.

(c) For any other meter, the qualifying duration is the recorded duration as it stands.

Rounding up leaves unchanged a recorded duration that already falls on a whole hour under (a), or on a quarter hour under (b).

**Where the measured duration acts.** The qualifying duration so measured is the figure compared with the minimum duration for the credit when deciding whether the record qualifies, and the figure from which the excess hours over that minimum are taken.

**Illustration (hypothetical recorded durations).**

| Recorded duration | 60-minute interval meter | 15-minute interval meter | Any other meter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30.2 hours | 31 hours | 30.25 hours | 30.2 hours |
| 19.6 hours | 20 hours | 19.75 hours | 19.6 hours |
| 18.0 hours | 18 hours | 18.0 hours | 18.0 hours |

With a hypothetical minimum duration of 20 hours, the 19.6-hour record reaches the minimum under a 60-minute interval meter (20 hours) and falls short under a 15-minute interval meter (19.75 hours) or any other meter (19.6 hours).

title: Care Desk Guidance Note: Electric Service Agreement Outage Records
content:
This guidance note states the rules the care desk applies to outage records under the **Electric Service Agreement**.

**Source of records.** Outage records are created by the outage management system, never from a customer's account of an outage.

**What is recorded.** One record is written for each interruption at the service address lasting 5 minutes or longer; momentary interruptions shorter than 5 minutes are not recorded and earn no credit.

| Interruption at the address (hypothetical) | Recorded? |
|---|---|
| 4 minutes | no; momentary, earns no credit |
| exactly 5 minutes | yes |
| 2 hours 15 minutes | yes |

**Duration.** The recorded duration in hours is the time from the outage start to the restoration time, rounded to one decimal place. Hypothetical: start 14:10, restoration 17:52; elapsed 3 hours 42 minutes, which is 3.7 hours. Start 08:00, restoration 08:20; elapsed 20 minutes, recorded as 0.3 hours.

**Major event day flag.** The major event day flag is true when the interruption began on a day the company declared a major event day under its reliability reporting method, and the flag is never changed afterwards. An interruption that began the day before a declared major event day and ran into it is not flagged, because the flag follows the day the interruption began.

**Reported outage with no record.** When a customer reports an outage that has no record at the address, no outage credit can be decided from the customer's account, and the request is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy so that field records can be reviewed.

title: Past-Due Balance and Notice-Avoidance Amount: Billing Operations Method for the Electric Service Agreement
content:
## Method statement

For an **Electric Service Agreement**, Billing Operations works the notice-avoidance amount as of the payment day as follows.

**1. Past-due balance.** The past-due balance is the sum of the agreement's bills whose due date has passed and all of its charges, less all of its payments and credits; a balance transferred from a closed agreement is left out until it is billed. Every bill of the agreement enters except the most recent bill, which enters only once its due date is before the payment day. A balance-transfer debit (a balance transferred onto the agreement from a closed agreement) is left out of the charges.

**2. Allowance.** The allowance is one cent (USD 0.01) under the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice.

**3. Notice-avoidance amount.** The notice-avoidance amount is the past-due balance less the allowance, never below zero, rounded to the cent. The floor at zero acts on that difference at the moment the allowance is subtracted, and rounding to the cent is the last operation.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

Hypothetical notice minimum USD 80.00, so the allowance is USD 79.99.

| Hypothetical record | USD |
|---|---|
| Two earlier bills | 140.00 and 96.50 |
| Most recent bill, due date after the payment day | 88.20 |
| Charges (one late payment charge) | 3.10 |
| Balance-transfer debit | 60.00 |
| Payments and credits | 120.00 |

- Past-due balance: 140.00 plus 96.50 plus 3.10, less 120.00, gives 119.60 (the most recent bill and the balance-transfer debit stay out).
- Notice-avoidance amount: 119.60 less 79.99 gives USD 39.61.

**Due-date boundary (hypothetical).** If the payment day is the most recent bill's due date, that bill still stays out and the amount is USD 39.61. If the payment day is the day after its due date, the bill enters: past-due balance 207.80, amount USD 127.81.

**Floor (hypothetical).** A past-due balance of USD 50.00 less 79.99 falls below zero, so the notice-avoidance amount is USD 0.00.

title: Billing Analyst Worked Examples: Payment Posting and Returned Payments on the Electric Service Agreement
content:
**Billing analyst worked-example sheet: posting payments and returned payments on an Electric Service Agreement**

## Rules applied

- **Posting.** A payment is posted on the date it is received, for the amount received, under the confirmation number issued by the payment channel.
- **Application.** Payments and credits are applied to the oldest unpaid charges first.
- **Returned payment.** A payment returned unpaid by the bank is reversed for its full amount, and the schedule's returned payment fee is posted the same day against the same payment. Each payment is reversed at most once.
- **Channel restriction.** When the number of returned payments posted on the account in the schedule's returned-payment look-back (that many calendar months ending on the handling date) reaches the schedule's returned-payment restriction count, payments by mailed check, online bank transfer and autopay are not accepted for the schedule's restriction period of months after the latest return. Card, authorized pay station cash and energy assistance agency payments remain accepted.
- **Energy assistance agencies.** A payment from an energy assistance agency is posted like any other payment and never attracts a returned payment fee.

## Clause no longer in force

The clause that each confirmation number is posted once is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

## Worked example 1 (hypothetical figures)

An account owes a bill charge of 80.00 dated 2 February and a bill charge of 95.00 dated 4 March. A payment of 120.00 received on 20 March is posted on 20 March for 120.00. It settles the 80.00 charge first and 40.00 of the 95.00 charge, leaving 55.00 of the March charge unpaid.

## Worked example 2 (hypothetical figures)

The 120.00 payment is returned unpaid by the bank on 2 April. On 2 April a reversal of 120.00 is posted, and the schedule's returned payment fee is posted the same day against that payment. A second reversal of the same payment does not arise.

## Worked example 3 (hypothetical figures)

*Hypothetical schedule figures for illustration only:* restriction count 2, look-back and restriction period 6 months. Returns posted on 2 April and 15 July; handling date 1 August. Two returns fall within the 6 calendar months ending 1 August, so the count is reached: mailed check, online bank transfer and autopay payments are not accepted for 6 months after 15 July, the latest return, while card, authorized pay station cash and energy assistance agency payments are still accepted. With only the 15 July return in the look-back, the count of 1 would not reach the restriction count.

title: Worked-Example Sheet: Load Margin by Measured Demand on Electric Service Agreement Payments
content:
**Electric Service Agreement.** A load margin is added to the notice-avoidance amount, set by the highest measured demand shown on the agreement's bills:

- **20 kW or more** — 0.2 times the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice;
- **at least 10 kW but below 20 kW** — 0.1 times that minimum;
- **below 10 kW** — nothing.

Every bill of the agreement is read for its measured demand, and the highest figure decides. The load margin is added after the allowance has been subtracted from the past-due balance and the difference held at no less than zero; the sum is then rounded to the cent.

## Worked examples (all inputs hypothetical; notice minimum USD 80.00, allowance USD 79.99)

| Example | Highest measured demand | Load margin | Past-due balance | Notice-avoidance amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34.6 kW | 16.00 | 150.00 | 70.01 plus 16.00, USD 86.01 |
| 2 | 20.0 kW | 16.00 | 50.00 | 0.00 plus 16.00, USD 16.00 |
| 3 | 19.9 kW | 8.00 | 150.00 | 70.01 plus 8.00, USD 78.01 |
| 4 | 10.0 kW | 8.00 | 50.00 | 0.00 plus 8.00, USD 8.00 |
| 5 | 9.8 kW | 0.00 | 150.00 | USD 70.01 |

Examples 2 and 4 show the margin added to a difference already held at zero. Examples 2 and 3, and 4 and 5, sit on either side of the 20 kW and 10 kW thresholds.

title: Revenue Recovery Bulletin: Unpaid Final-Bill Balances on Closed Electric Service Agreements
content:
**Final Accounts Unit, Revenue Recovery: balances left on closed Electric Service Agreements**

Under the Electric Service Agreement, balances follow the customer, not the address. This bulletin states the terms that govern an unpaid final-bill balance left on a closed agreement.

## Terms in force

**Ageing of the final bill.** A transfer is made only when the final bill of the closed agreement has remained unpaid for at least the prior balance transfer period after its due date. The period is counted in calendar days, starting the day after the final bill's due date, and the transfer may be made on the day the count reaches the period, not before. The period that applies is the value set by the closed agreement's own schedule. The test reads the company's bill records for the closed agreement (its final bill and that bill's due date).

**Receiving agreement.** The receiving agreement is the same customer's open agreement (active, notice pending or disconnected) with the earliest start date. When the customer has no open agreement, the balance stays on the closed agreement.

**Credit balances.** A credit balance is never transferred; it is refunded under the company's stop-service and final-bill terms.

## Time test, worked on both sides (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical figures, chosen for illustration only:* a closed agreement whose schedule sets a period of 20 days, and a final bill due on 1 April that remains unpaid.

| Date | Day of the count | Transfer permitted? |
|---|---|---|
| 2 April | day 1 | no |
| 20 April | day 19 (the day before the count reaches the period) | no |
| 21 April | day 20 (the count reaches the period) | yes |
| 22 April | day 21 | yes |

## Receiving agreement (hypothetical)

A customer's open agreements started on 3 March 2021 (active) and on 9 June 2019 (disconnected). The receiving agreement is the one started on 9 June 2019: disconnected status counts as open, and the earliest start date decides.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of these terms are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- the clause that an unpaid final-bill balance left on a closed agreement is transferred to an open agreement of the same customer;
- the clause that the transfer posts two entries for the whole unpaid balance of the closed agreement on the same posting date, namely a prior balance transfer program credit on the closed agreement referencing the receiving agreement and a prior balance transfer program debit on the receiving agreement referencing the closed agreement;
- the clause that a transferred balance becomes part of the receiving agreement's next bill cycle and is past due on that agreement only after that bill's due date.

title: Care Desk Tool Reference Card: Electric Service Agreement Prior Balance Transfer
content:
## Rule this tool books

Under the **Electric Service Agreement**, a balance transfer moves the unpaid balance of a closed agreement onto the customer's open agreement with the earliest start date: a transfer debit on the receiving agreement for the transfer amount, and a transfer credit on the closed agreement that clears its recorded balance, both dated the transfer day. The closed agreement's schedule supplies every rate, fee and period used.

In the records, the transfer appears as a **balance transfer credit** on the closed agreement and a **balance-transfer debit** on the receiving agreement, each naming the other agreement as its source. After the transfer the closed agreement's balance stands at zero and the receiving agreement's balance owed is higher by the transfer amount.

## Invocation

The tool is `transfer_prior_balance_e8000638`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the open agreement that receives the balance, as returned by the service agreement lookup | identifier |
| `source_reference_id` | The service account number of the closed agreement whose balance is transferred, as returned by the service agreement lookup | identifier |
| `amount` | The transfer amount debited to the receiving agreement, in USD | positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); a value with more decimals is rounded half-up to the cent when booked |

The balance transfer credit on the closed agreement is not a parameter: it is always booked for the closed agreement's recorded balance.

## Return

A confirmation sentence stating the transfer debit reference number (an opaque id beginning `pbd_`) and its amount in USD to 2 decimal places, the transfer credit reference number (an opaque id beginning `pbc_`) and the amount cleared from the closed agreement in USD to 2 decimal places, the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD), and both agreements' new balances in USD to 2 decimal places. Receiving this sentence means both entries are posted.

title: Quick Reference Card: Program Amounts on the Electric Service Agreement Ledger
content:
**Electric Service Agreement: amounts decided in another program.**

**Posting rule.** Amounts decided in another program are posted to the service agreement named on the originating record, for exactly the originating record's amount, on the originating record's date, with the originating record's identifier as the posting's source reference and the charge code or credit code that names the program entry. Each originating record is posted once per code.

| Originating record | Posting on the agreement |
|---|---|
| Meter accuracy adjustment that refunds overbilling | billing credit, meter error refund code |
| Meter accuracy adjustment that recovers underbilling | backbill charge, reason slow meter |
| Energy found used through confirmed tampering or diversion | backbill charge, reason unauthorized use |
| Corrected estimated reading | the difference, as a backbill charge with reason estimated-read true-up (an amount the customer owes) or as a billing credit with the billing error correction code (an amount owed to the customer) |
| Any other program entry | program charge or program credit under the code naming that entry |

**Status of the receiving agreement.** Program postings are accepted on an agreement in any status except pending start, so that a closed agreement can still receive deposit applications and final program amounts.

| Agreement status | Program posting accepted? |
|---|---|
| pending start | no |
| active | yes |
| notice pending | yes |
| disconnected | yes |
| closed | yes |

**Points of judgement (hypothetical).**
- An originating record dated 12 August for 86.40 USD, naming agreement A, posts 86.40 USD to agreement A dated 12 August, whatever day the posting is made.
- If that record already appears on agreement A under the same code, it is not posted again; a posting under a different code that names a different program entry is a separate posting.

title: Terms and Conditions of Service: Rate Schedule Changes Under an Electric Service Agreement
content:
**Terms and conditions of service, Lakeshore Power & Light Company: moving an Electric Service Agreement to another rate schedule**

**1. Right to change.** The customer may move an Electric Service Agreement that is active or notice pending to another schedule of the same customer type (residential or business) whose entry requirements the service address meets. The same demand, communicating-meter and vehicle tests apply as when an agreement is opened.

**2. Agreements that cannot be changed.** A change requested on a closed, disconnected or pending start agreement is not made. The company reads the agreement's status from its own records.

**3. Lockout period.** A schedule change is accepted only when the rate change lockout period has elapsed since the current schedule's effective date. The lockout is the value set by the current schedule. Months are counted as calendar months from the rate effective date, and when the target month is shorter, the boundary falls on its last day. A request made on the boundary day is accepted; a request made before it is not.

**4. Return within bill protection.** The lockout does not apply when a customer still inside the bill-protection period of Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service or Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service returns to Schedule RS Residential Standard Service, or when a customer still inside the bill-protection period of Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service returns to Schedule GS Small General Service.

**5. Effective date.** The new schedule takes effect on the first day after the billing period end of the most recent regular bill, and that date becomes the agreement's rate effective date. No bill is recalculated retroactively.

## Lockout boundary (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical figures for illustration only:* a current schedule whose lockout is 6 months, and a rate effective date of 31 August 2025. Six calendar months later is February 2026, which has no 31st, so the boundary falls on 28 February 2026.

| Request date | Lockout elapsed? |
|---|---|
| 27 February 2026 (the day before the boundary) | no; the change is not accepted |
| 28 February 2026 (the boundary day) | yes; the change is accepted |

## Effective date (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical:* the most recent regular bill covered a billing period ending on 14 May. An accepted change takes effect on 15 May, which is written as the new rate effective date; the bill for the period ending 14 May stays as issued.

title: Card Payments toward Reconnection of a Disconnected Electric Service Agreement
content:
When a disconnected agreement is to be reconnected on payment, the customer pays the reconnection payment amount by card on the call, and the payment is posted that day under the confirmation number the card processor issues when it authorizes the payment. A card payment taken on the call is posted once, under the one confirmation number its authorization produces.

This desk guidance governs that payment on an Electric Service Agreement of Lakeshore Power & Light Company: the amount paid is the reconnection payment amount, the channel is a debit or credit card, and the payment is posted on the day it is taken.

## When the amount is fixed

The reconnection payment amount is fixed only after the agreement carries a late payment charge on its most recent bill once that bill's grace period has ended with part of it unpaid.

The reconnection payment amount is not fixed until the agreement carries the sustained-outage credit owed for the most recent outage record at its service address when that record qualifies.

In terms of the agreement's records: while the most recent bill's grace period has ended with part of that bill unpaid and the agreement carries no late payment charge on that bill, the reconnection payment amount is not yet fixed; and while the most recent outage record at the service address qualifies and the agreement carries no sustained-outage credit for that record, the reconnection payment amount is not yet fixed.

## The card payment tool

The payment is made with `take_card_payment_dce85fc7`, a customer-side tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, authorizing a one-time card payment of the stated amount on the agreement. The card processor issues a confirmation number at authorization; the payment is posted to the agreement that day under that number through the card channel, and the agreement's balance owed falls by the amount paid. The customer can read the confirmation number back at once, and the payment shows on the account immediately.

**Parameters**

- `service_account_id` — the service account number of the Electric Service Agreement the customer is paying, as the agent reads it out from the service agreement lookup. Identifier.
- `amount` — the payment amount in USD: a positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); a value with more decimals is rounded half-up to the cent when it is posted.

**Return.** A confirmation sentence stating the card payment confirmation number (an opaque reference beginning "CRD-"), the amount paid in USD with 2 decimal places, the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the agreement's new balance owed in USD with 2 decimal places. Receiving this sentence means the payment is posted.

title: Electric Service Agreement Reconnection Charge — Amount Charged on a Reconnection Order
content:
Field Services states the reconnection charge posted with a reconnection order on an Electric Service Agreement as follows.

> The reconnection charge is the schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours, rounded to the cent.

The charge is figured once for the order, from the schedule the agreement is billed under, and only the final reconnection charge is rounded to the cent. It is a single charge, dated the order date.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Hypothetical schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours | Reconnection charge posted |
|---|---|
| 85.00 USD | 85.00 USD |
| 140.00 USD | 140.00 USD |

The schedule's figure is read from the reconnection charge values of the schedule; the charge posted is that figure stated to the cent.

title: Electric Service Agreement Reconnection Charge for Households Receiving Energy Assistance — Decision Card
content:
**Decision rule.** The reconnection charge on an Electric Service Agreement is multiplied by a hardship share of one half (0.5) when the agreement received two or more payments from an energy assistance agency in the assistance window, three quarters (0.75) when it received exactly one such payment there, and one when it received none. The share multiplies the reconnection charge before it is rounded; only the final reconnection charge is rounded to the cent.

**Payments counted.** Payments posted to the agreement through the energy assistance agency channel and dated within the assistance window, which is counted back from the order date.

| Agency payments in the assistance window | Hardship share | Hypothetical charge of 140.00 USD becomes |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | 0.5 | 70.00 |
| exactly 1 | 0.75 | 105.00 |
| none | 1 | 140.00 |

**Either side of each line.** One payment gives 0.75 and a second gives 0.5; with no payment in the window the charge is not reduced. A payment dated before the assistance window does not count.

title: Long-Standing Electric Service Agreements: Reduced Reconnection Charge
content:
**Term.** The reconnection charge is multiplied by a tenure share of 0.8 for an Electric Service Agreement in service 120 whole calendar months or more since its start date, 0.9 for one in service at least 60 but fewer than 120 months, and 1 for one in service fewer than 60 months. The share multiplies the reconnection charge before it is rounded; only the final reconnection charge is rounded to the cent.

**Months in service.** Whole calendar months from the agreement's start date to the order date; a month not completed is not counted.

| Whole calendar months in service | Tenure share |
|---|---|
| 120 or more | 0.8 |
| 60 to 119 | 0.9 |
| fewer than 60 | 1 |

**On either side of the thresholds (hypothetical agreements).**

- In service 119 whole months: share 0.9. In service 120 whole months: share 0.8.
- In service 59 whole months: share 1. In service 60 whole months: share 0.9.

**Example (hypothetical figures).** A reconnection charge of 65.00 USD on an agreement started 12 years before the order becomes 52.00 USD (65.00 times 0.8); on one started 7 years before, it becomes 58.50 USD (65.00 times 0.9); on one started 3 years before, it stays 65.00 USD.

title: Electric Service Agreement Reconnection Charges and Standard Reconnection Hours
content:
Field Services and Credit & Collections apply the following reconnection values for each Electric Service Agreement rate schedule.

## The three reconnection charges

- **Remote reconnection charge** — the charge when service is restored remotely through a remote-switch-capable meter.
- **Field reconnection charge for standard hours** — the charge when a field crew restores service during standard reconnection hours.
- **After-hours field reconnection charge** — the charge when the customer elects same-day field restoration outside standard reconnection hours.

## Charges by schedule

Columns: RS is Schedule RS Residential Standard Service, RT is Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service, REV is Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service, GS is Schedule GS Small General Service, GST is Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service, GD is Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service and LP is Schedule LP Large Power Service.

| Term | RS | RT | REV | GS | GST | GD | LP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remote reconnection charge, USD | 10.00 | 10.00 | 10.00 | 10.00 | 10.00 | 25.00 | 25.00 |
| Field reconnection charge, standard hours, USD | 65.00 | 65.00 | 65.00 | 85.00 | 85.00 | 140.00 | 285.00 |

| Reconnection payment basis | past-due balance | past-due balance | past-due balance | whole account balance | whole account balance | whole account balance | whole account balance |

**Standard reconnection hours** — the clock window in which reconnection orders are worked at the standard charge — are 08:00-17:00 Monday-Friday except company holidays on every schedule.

**Reconnection payment basis** — the amount that must be paid before a disconnected account is reconnected without an arrangement or protection: the past-due balance on the residential schedules (RS, RT, REV) and the whole account balance on the business schedules (GS, GST, GD, LP).

## Reading across the schedule

title: Good-Faith Add-On in the Reconnection Payment after Written Disconnection Notices — Electric Service Agreement Training
content:
Questions answered for desk staff on the good-faith add-on in the reconnection payment of a disconnected Electric Service Agreement.

**What is the rule?** A good-faith add-on is included in the reconnection payment: the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice when three or more written disconnection notices were served on the agreement in the 12 calendar months before the payment, half (0.5 times) of that minimum when exactly two were, and nothing when one or none was.

**Where does it enter the payment?** It is added to the reconnection payment after the basis amount has been rounded to the cent.

**Which notices count?** Written disconnection notices served on the same agreement. Final notices by phone call or door hanger are not written notices. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date.

**What figure is used?** The minimum past-due balance for a written disconnection notice of the schedule the agreement is billed under.

| Written disconnection notices in the 12 calendar months before the payment | Good-faith add-on |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice |
| exactly 2 | half of that minimum |
| 1 or none | nothing |

**Worked question (hypothetical figures).** On a hypothetical schedule whose minimum past-due balance for a notice is 250.00 USD, two written notices in the period give an add-on of 125.00 USD and three give 250.00 USD. If the basis amount, rounded to the cent, were 310.40 USD, the payment would include 435.40 USD and 560.40 USD respectively.

title: Reconnection Orders for Disconnected Electric Service Agreements
content:
A reconnection order restores a disconnected agreement to active status on the order date and posts one reconnection charge dated that day, recording the restoration method and the order timing.

The clauses below apply to every reconnection order on an Electric Service Agreement of Lakeshore Power & Light Company.

## Conditions of the order

1. A reconnection order that rests on payment is issued only after the card, authorized pay station cash and energy assistance agency payments posted to the agreement since its disconnection date add up to at least the reconnection payment amount.
2. Put the other way round, for a reconnection that rests on payment: while the card, authorized pay station cash and energy assistance agency payments posted to the agreement since its disconnection date add up to less than the reconnection payment amount, no reconnection order is issued.
3. Payments by mail check, online bank transfer or autopay do not count toward a reconnection that rests on payment, because they can still be returned unpaid.
4. A reconnection order that rests on an active payment arrangement on the agreement whose down payment has been received, or on an active medical certification for the agreement whose kind requires disconnected service to be restored, needs no payment.
5. The order timing is standard hours when the order is placed within the schedule's standard reconnection hours, and after hours otherwise.

| Payment posted since the disconnection date through | Counts toward a reconnection that rests on payment |
|---|---|
| card | yes |
| authorized pay station cash | yes |
| energy assistance agency | yes |
| mail check | no |
| online bank transfer | no |
| autopay | no |

## Issuing the order

The order is issued with `issue_reconnection_order_52263bc7`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. The order moves the agreement back to active status with the order date as its latest status date and, when the reconnection charge is above zero, books one reconnection charge dated that day recording how service is restored and when the order is worked; the agreement's balance owed rises by that charge. The customer sees the agreement as active and the charge on the account at once.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the disconnected Electric Service Agreement to restore, as returned by the service agreement lookup. Identifier. |
| `reconnection_charge` | The reconnection charge in USD: a number of 0 or more with 2 decimal places (cents); 0.00 books no charge; a value with more decimals is rounded half-up to the cent. |
| `reconnect_method` | How service is restored, exactly one of: `remote` (service is switched back on through the remote switch of the meter in service), `field` (a crew restores service at the premise), `not_applicable` (never used on a reconnection order; the value exists only for charges of other kinds). |
| `reconnect_timing` | When the order is worked, exactly one of: `standard_hours` (the order is placed and worked within the standard reconnection hours), `after_hours` (the order is placed outside the standard reconnection hours for same-day restoration), `not_applicable` (never used on a reconnection order; the value exists only for charges of other kinds). |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence stating the agreement's new status (active), the status date (YYYY-MM-DD), the reconnection charge reference number (an opaque identifier beginning "rcc_", or "none" when the charge is 0.00), the charge in USD with 2 decimal places, the restoration method and timing, and the agreement's new balance owed in USD with 2 decimal places. Receiving this sentence means the order is issued.

title: Electric Service Agreement Reconnection Payment Amount — Worked Examples
content:
This sheet works the reconnection payment amount of a disconnected Electric Service Agreement through to a figure.

## The calculation

The agreement's balance is the sum of its bills and charges less the sum of its payments and credits. The reconnection payment amount is that balance less every late payment charge ever posted on the agreement, rounded to the cent. The amount so reached is never below zero: where the late payment charges exceed the balance, the reconnection payment amount is 0.00.

In words, the inputs are:

| Input | Taken from the agreement's records |
|---|---|
| Bills | every bill issued on the agreement, regular and final |
| Charges | every charge posted on the agreement, late payment charges included |
| Payments and credits | every payment and every credit posted on the agreement |
| Late payment charges | every late payment charge ever posted on the agreement |

## Example 1 (hypothetical figures)

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Bills | 1,240.50 |
| Charges (of which late payment charges 12.40) | 86.00 |
| Payments and credits | 905.25 |
| Balance: 1,240.50 plus 86.00 less 905.25 | 421.25 |
| Less every late payment charge ever posted | 12.40 |
| Reconnection payment amount | 408.85 |

## Example 2 (hypothetical figures)

Bills of 610.00, charges of 22.80 (all of them late payment charges) and payments and credits of 610.00 give a balance of 22.80. Less the 22.80 of late payment charges the amount is 0.00.

## Example 3 (hypothetical figures)

Bills of 300.00, charges of 15.00 (all late payment charges) and payments and credits of 296.00 give a balance of 19.00. Less the 15.00 of late payment charges the amount is 4.00.

## Example 4 (hypothetical figures)

Bills of 300.00, charges of 15.00 (all late payment charges) and payments and credits of 310.00 give a balance of 5.00. Less the 15.00 of late payment charges the figure would fall below zero, so the reconnection payment amount is 0.00.

title: Reconnection History and the Basis of the Reconnection Payment on an Electric Service Agreement
content:
## Provision

The basis of the reconnection payment for a disconnected Electric Service Agreement depends on the reconnection charges posted on the agreement in the 24 calendar months before the payment: with two or more, the basis is the whole balance; with exactly one, the basis is the balance less the late payment charges posted 12 or more calendar months before the payment; with none, the basis is the balance less every late payment charge ever posted on the agreement.

The balance is the sum of the agreement's bills and charges less the sum of its payments and credits. Every count or sum over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date: a reconnection charge counts toward the 24 months when it is dated less than 24 whole calendar months before the payment, and a late payment charge is one of those posted 12 or more calendar months before the payment when it is not dated less than 12 whole calendar months before it.

## Basis by history

| Reconnection charges on the agreement in the 24 calendar months before the payment | Basis of the reconnection payment |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | the whole balance |
| exactly 1 | the balance less the late payment charges posted 12 or more calendar months before the payment |
| none | the balance less every late payment charge ever posted on the agreement |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

An agreement has a balance of 640.00 USD. Its late payment charges total 48.00 USD, of which 30.00 USD were posted 12 or more calendar months before the payment and 18.00 USD less than 12 whole calendar months before it.

- With no reconnection charge in the 24 months, the basis is 640.00 less 48.00, that is 592.00.
- With exactly one, the basis is 640.00 less 30.00, that is 610.00; the 18.00 of recent late payment charges stay in the basis.
- With two or more, the basis is the whole 640.00.

The boundary lies between one and two reconnection charges, and between none and one.

title: Hardship Share of the Reconnection Payment for Electric Service Agreements Supported by Energy Assistance Agencies
content:
**Clause 1 — Share.** The basis of the reconnection payment for a disconnected Electric Service Agreement is multiplied by a hardship share of 0.6 when the agreement received two or more payments from an energy assistance agency in the 12 calendar months before the payment, 0.8 when it received exactly one such payment, and 1 when it received none.

**Clause 2 — Point of action.** The hardship share multiplies the basis, taken never below zero, before that amount is rounded to the cent; the share is not rounded on its own.

**Clause 3 — Payments counted.** The payments counted are those posted to the agreement through the energy assistance agency channel. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date.

| Energy assistance agency payments in the 12 calendar months before the payment | Hardship share |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 0.6 |
| exactly 1 | 0.8 |
| none | 1 |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** One agency payment dated less than 12 whole calendar months before the payment and another dated exactly 12 whole calendar months before it: only the first counts, so the share is 0.8. Both dated within the 12 months: the share is 0.6.

**Illustration (hypothetical figures).** A basis of 455.00 USD with exactly one agency payment in the period is multiplied by 0.8, giving 364.00 USD; with two or more it is multiplied by 0.6, giving 273.00 USD; with none it stays 455.00 USD.

title: Length of Service and the Reconnection Payment — Electric Service Agreement Quick Reference
content:
**Electric Service Agreement — reconnection payment, length of service.**

The basis of the reconnection payment is also multiplied by a tenure share of 0.9 for an agreement in service 120 whole calendar months or more since its start date, 0.95 for one in service at least 60 but fewer than 120 months, and 1 for one in service fewer than 60 months. The tenure share multiplies the basis, taken never below zero, before that amount is rounded to the cent.

| Whole calendar months in service, from the agreement's start date to the payment | Tenure share |
|---|---|
| 120 or more | 0.9 |
| 60 to 119 | 0.95 |
| fewer than 60 | 1 |

**Counting months.** Months in service are whole calendar months from the agreement's start date to the day of the payment; a month that has not been completed is not counted.

**Either side of each threshold (hypothetical).**

- 119 whole months: 0.95. 120 whole months: 0.9.
- 59 whole months: 1. 60 whole months: 0.95.

**Example (hypothetical figures).** An agreement started 10 years and 2 months before the payment has 122 whole months in service; a basis of 380.00 USD becomes 342.00 USD (380.00 times 0.9). Started 5 years before the payment to the day, it has 60 whole months and the basis becomes 361.00 USD (380.00 times 0.95).

title: Collections Manual: Reconnecting a Disconnected Electric Service Agreement
content:
**Credit & Collections manual section: reconnection of the Electric Service Agreement.**

A disconnected agreement is reconnected when one of the following holds. Reconnection is ordered only after the reconnection payment requirement is met or an alternative listed below applies. Whether either holds is read from the company's records for that agreement: the payments posted to it and the date it was disconnected.

### Alternatives to the payment requirement
The alternatives are an active payment arrangement on the agreement whose down payment has been received, or an active medical certification for the agreement whose kind requires disconnected service to be restored. The arrangement is a Payment Arrangement record and the certification a Medical and Life-Support Protections record, each for the same agreement.

| Record held on the agreement (hypothetical) | Alternative available? |
|---|---|
| Active payment arrangement, down payment received | yes |
| Active payment arrangement, down payment not yet received | no |
| Active medical certification of a kind that requires disconnected service to be restored | yes |

### Retired clause on meeting the payment requirement
The clause under which the payment requirement was met when payments posted since the disconnection date reached the schedule's reconnection payment basis measured at disconnection (the past-due balance for residential schedules, the whole account balance for business schedules) is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

### Reconnection charge
- A reconnection under such a medical certification whose kind waives the reconnection charge, or a reconnection of a disconnection performed without a valid pending notice, carries no reconnection charge.
- Every other reconnection posts exactly one reconnection charge dated the reconnection order date.
- The reconnection charge is posted only on an agreement that has been restored to active status, so the charge is not posted while the agreement is still disconnected.
- The clause that set the amount of the charge by whether the in-service meter is remote-switch capable under its metering type, and otherwise by standard-hours or elected after-hours same-day field restoration, is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

### Deposit
A residential reconnection after disconnection for nonpayment is also subject to the reestablishment deposit rules of the Security Deposit program.

title: Restoration Path and Charge for Reconnecting an Electric Service Agreement — Metering and Field Findings
content:
**Restoration charge.** For a reconnection order on an Electric Service Agreement, the restoration charge is the schedule's remote reconnection charge when the meter in service at the premise is remote-switch capable and no tampering or diversion finding was confirmed at the premise in the 24 calendar months before the order, a tampering investigation that found no tampering or could not gain access not being such a finding; it is the schedule's after-hours field reconnection charge when such a finding was confirmed in that period and a meter is in service at the premise, because service is then restored by a line crew at the pole; in every other case it is the schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours. The restoration charge is the amount the reconnection charge rests on.

**Restoration method.** The restoration method recorded with the charge is remote when the remote reconnection charge applies and field otherwise.

**Records read.** Both conditions are read from the Metering Service records of the premise: the meter installation in service there, whose meter type shows whether it is remote-switch capable, and the field investigation orders at the premise with their tampering findings. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date, so a finding counts when its order is dated less than 24 whole calendar months before the reconnection order. An investigation recorded as finding no tampering, or as unable to gain access, is not a confirmed finding.

## Combinations

| Meter in service at the premise | Tampering or diversion finding confirmed in the 24 months | Restoration charge | Method recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| remote-switch capable | no | schedule's remote reconnection charge | remote |
| remote-switch capable | yes | schedule's after-hours field reconnection charge | field |
| not remote-switch capable | no | schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours | field |
| not remote-switch capable | yes | schedule's after-hours field reconnection charge | field |
| no meter in service | no | schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours | field |
| no meter in service | yes | schedule's field reconnection charge for standard hours | field |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A premise whose remote-switch-capable meter is in service had an investigation 9 months before the order that could not gain access: that is not a finding, so the remote reconnection charge applies and the method recorded is remote. Had the investigation confirmed diversion, the after-hours field reconnection charge would apply and the method recorded would be field.

title: Returned Payments and the Reconnection Payment — Electric Service Agreement Terms of Service
content:
Under the terms of the Electric Service Agreement, a customer whose payments have recently been returned unpaid pays a returned-payment add-on as part of the reconnection payment.

**Term.** A returned-payment add-on is included in the reconnection payment: five times (5 times) the schedule's returned payment fee when two or more payments on the agreement were reversed as returned unpaid in the 12 calendar months before the payment, two and a half times (2.5 times) that fee when exactly one was, and nothing when none was.

**How it is added.** The add-on is added to the reconnection payment after the basis amount has been rounded to the cent. The payment total is stated rounded to the cent.

**Returns counted.** Payments on the agreement reversed as returned unpaid by the customer's bank. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date.

| Payments reversed as returned unpaid in the 12 calendar months before the payment | Returned-payment add-on |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 5 times the schedule's returned payment fee |
| exactly 1 | 2.5 times the schedule's returned payment fee |
| none | nothing |

**Illustration (hypothetical figures).** With a hypothetical returned payment fee of 25.00 USD, one return in the period adds 62.50 USD and two or more add 125.00 USD. With no return, nothing is added.

title: Residential Reestablishment Deposit Status and the Electric Service Agreement Reconnection Charge — Training Notes
content:
Training notes on how a Residential Reestablishment Deposit held under the Security Deposit program bears on the reconnection charge of an Electric Service Agreement.

**The rule.** The reconnection charge is multiplied by a deposit share of one half (0.5) when the customer holds a fully secured Residential Reestablishment Deposit, three quarters (0.75) when such a deposit is still assessed and at least one deposit payment was received less than one whole calendar month before the order, and one in every other case. The share multiplies the reconnection charge before it is rounded; only the final reconnection charge is rounded to the cent.

**Which records decide it?** The customer's Security Deposit records: the Residential Reestablishment Deposit and its status — held once it is fully secured, assessed while it is still being paid — and the deposit payments recorded on the customer's deposits with their dates.

**What counts as recent?** A deposit payment dated less than one whole calendar month before the order. A payment dated exactly one whole calendar month before the order is not recent.

| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | Deposit payment less than one whole calendar month before the order | Deposit share |
|---|---|---|
| held (fully secured) | either | 0.5 |
| assessed (still being paid) | yes | 0.75 |
| assessed (still being paid) | no | 1 |
| none, or in any other status | either | 1 |

**Worked question (hypothetical figures).** A reconnection charge of 85.00 USD for a customer whose Residential Reestablishment Deposit is held becomes 42.50 USD. If the deposit were still assessed and a deposit payment had been received 10 days before the order, the charge would become 63.75 USD; with the last deposit payment two months before the order, it stays 85.00 USD.

title: Rate of the Late Payment Charge after Repeated Lateness — Electric Service Agreement Tariff Provision
content:
**1.** The rate for the late payment charge on an Electric Service Agreement bill is one and a half times (1.5 times) the schedule's late payment charge rate when three or more late payment charges were posted on the agreement in the repeat-lateness window, one and a quarter times (1.25 times) that rate when one or two were, and the schedule's late payment charge rate when none was.

**2.** The repeat-lateness window is a stated number of calendar months before the late payment charge now being posted. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. The late payment charges counted are those already posted on the same agreement; the charge now being posted is not among them.

**3.** The rate so found is the rate applied to the unpaid portion of the bill.

## Ladder

| Late payment charges posted on the agreement in the repeat-lateness window | Rate for the late payment charge |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 1.5 times the schedule's late payment charge rate |
| 1 or 2 | 1.25 times the schedule's late payment charge rate |
| 0 | the schedule's late payment charge rate |

## Boundaries shown on both sides

- 2 late payment charges in the window: 1.25 times the rate. 3 late payment charges: 1.5 times the rate.
- 0 late payment charges: the schedule's rate as it stands. 1 late payment charge: 1.25 times the rate.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

On a hypothetical schedule rate of 1.5%, an agreement with 1 late payment charge in the repeat-lateness window is charged at 1.875% (1.25 times 1.5%), and one with 4 such charges at 2.25% (1.5 times 1.5%). With 0 such charges the rate stays 1.5%.

title: Credit and Collections Manual: Returned-Payment History and the Allowance Under the Disconnection Notice Minimum
content:
## Section rule

For a payment made on an **Electric Service Agreement** toward the past-due minimum for a written disconnection notice, the allowance under the notice minimum is set by the payments on the agreement that were reversed as returned unpaid in the 24 calendar months before the payment:

| Payments reversed as returned unpaid in the 24 months | Allowance under the notice minimum |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | nothing (USD 0.00) |
| exactly 1 | half (0.5) of the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice, rounded to the cent |
| none | one cent (USD 0.01) under the schedule's minimum past-due balance for a disconnection notice |

The allowance is subtracted from the past-due balance.

## Counting returned payments

A returned payment is a payment on the agreement reversed as returned unpaid; each reversal counts once. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date; the posting here is the payment.

- Hypothetical: payment on 20 June; a reversal dated 20 June two years earlier is exactly 24 whole calendar months before and is not counted.
- Hypothetical: a reversal dated 21 June two years earlier is counted.

## Illustration (hypothetical notice minimum USD 80.00)

- Two reversals in the window: allowance USD 0.00.
- One reversal: allowance USD 40.00.
- No reversal: allowance USD 79.99.

title: Electric Service Agreement Rate Schedules: Customer Charge, Energy Rates and Power Supply Cost Recovery
content:
Lakeshore Power & Light Company prices every Electric Service Agreement under one of seven rate schedules. This price sheet states, for each schedule, the fixed monthly customer charge, the seasonal energy rates, the time-of-use periods and the Power Supply Cost Recovery factor.

## Terms of the price sheet

- **Customer charge.** A fixed monthly charge billed on every bill of the schedule, including first and final bills; it is not prorated.
- **Season.** A bill is a summer-season bill when the month of its billing-period end date is one of the schedule's summer billing months (two-digit months); every other bill is a winter-season bill.
- **On-peak and off-peak rates.** On-peak kWh are priced at the season's on-peak rate and off-peak kWh at the season's off-peak rate. A flat schedule has no on-peak window (shown as "none"): every kWh is billed at the season rate, and its off-peak rate equals its on-peak rate.
- **Super off-peak rate.** A year-round rate for kWh metered in the super off-peak window; it is 0.00000 on schedules whose super off-peak window is "none".
- **Power Supply Cost Recovery factor.** Charged on every billed kWh.

## Rates by schedule

## Time-of-use windows

- **Schedule RS Residential Standard Service**: on-peak hours none; super off-peak hours none.
- **Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service**: on-peak hours 15:00-20:00 Monday-Friday except company holidays; super off-peak hours none.
- **Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service**: on-peak hours 15:00-20:00 Monday-Friday except company holidays; super off-peak hours 00:00-06:00 every day.

title: Electric Service Agreement Start Orders: Schedule Assignment Decision Table
content:
**Quick reference card: opening an Electric Service Agreement and assigning its rate schedule**

## What a start order names

A start order for an Electric Service Agreement names the service address, the start date, the premise's primary space-heating source and its delivery voltage.

## Schedule by customer type and demand

The schedule must match the customer's type. Residential customers take Schedule RS Residential Standard Service, Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service or Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service. Business customers take Schedule GS Small General Service, Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service, Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service or Schedule LP Large Power Service.

Among the business schedules, the schedule is fixed by the highest measured demand on the address's bills in the 12 billing periods before the start date. For an address with no bill history, the customer's stated connected-load estimate is used instead.

| Highest measured demand (or stated connected-load estimate) | Business schedule |
|---|---|
| under 25 kW | Schedule GS or Schedule GST |
| 25 kW up to but excluding 500 kW | Schedule GD |
| 500 kW and above | Schedule LP |

*Hypothetical boundary readings:* 24.9 kW falls under Schedule GS or GST; exactly 25 kW falls under Schedule GD; 499.9 kW falls under Schedule GD; exactly 500 kW falls under Schedule LP.

## Additional entry requirements

| Schedule | Communicating smart meter at the address | Vehicle identification number |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule RT, Schedule GST | required | not required |
| Schedule REV | required | required |
| Schedule RS, GS, GD, LP | not required | not required |

A communicating smart meter is any meter installation in service at the address, in the Metering Service records, whose type is not the Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter. For Schedule REV the customer must supply the vehicle identification number of a plug-in electric vehicle registered at the service address; this is a fact the customer states.

## Start date

The start date may not be earlier than the next business day after the start order. Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding the company holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

*Hypothetical:* a start order placed on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving. Thanksgiving Day and the day after are company holidays, so the earliest start date is the following Monday; a start dated the Friday is too early.

## Opening and the connection charge

The agreement opens in pending start and is activated by the system on the start date. The connection charge of the assigned schedule is posted with the start date as its posting date. The connection charge is posted only on an agreement in pending start or active status. It is not posted for a residential customer whose income-qualified-until date is on or after the start date.

title: Terms and Conditions of Electric Service: Stopping Service, Final Bills and Credit Refunds
content:
These terms of the **Electric Service Agreement** set out how an agreement with Lakeshore Power & Light Company is stopped, cancelled or closed, and how a closed agreement is final-billed and refunded.

**1. Who may stop service.** Only the customer of record can stop service or cancel a start. The company's agent records the request as a stop-service order or a cancel-start order awaiting the customer's confirmation, and the agreement closes only when the customer confirms.

**2. Stop effective date.** The stop effective date must be at least the schedule's minimum stop notice in business days after the request date, counting business days as Monday through Friday excluding company holidays; an earlier date is moved to the first permitted date. A date exactly that many business days after the request date is permitted; one business day earlier is moved. Hypothetical illustration with a minimum of two business days and no holiday: for a Thursday request, Friday is business day one and Monday business day two, so a Friday date moves to Monday and a Monday or later date stands.

**3. Cancelling a start.** A start can be cancelled only while the agreement is pending start; once it is active, cancellation of the start is no longer available.

**4. Closure of a disconnected agreement.** A disconnected agreement not reconnected within the schedule's disconnected-closure period, in calendar days after the disconnection date, is closed by the system on the day after that period ends. Hypothetically, with disconnection on 1 May and a period of 30 days, the period ends on 31 May and the agreement closes on 1 June unless it was reconnected by 31 May.

**5. Final bill.** Every closure issues a final bill within the schedule's final bill issue period in business days.

**6. Deposit and refund.** Any security deposit held is applied to the final bill under the Security Deposit program before a refund is considered. A credit balance remaining on a closed agreement after the final bill and deposit application is refunded by check when it is at least the schedule's credit refund minimum. A refund is issued only on a closed agreement whose balance is below zero, and only for the whole credit balance; no partial refund is made, and an agreement that is not closed receives no refund.

title: Sustained-Outage Credit Amount under the Electric Service Agreement — Method Statement and Worked Figures
content:
Billing Operations sets out here how the amount of a sustained-outage credit on an **Electric Service Agreement** of Lakeshore Power & Light Company is worked to a figure.

## Method

1. **Record assessed.** The record assessed is the most recent outage record at the agreement's service address, that is, the record whose outage began latest.
2. **Qualifying duration.** The qualifying duration of the record is its recorded duration in hours.
3. **Qualification.** The record qualifies when its qualifying duration is at least the schedule's minimum outage credit duration. An outage record does not qualify when it began on a major event day while the schedule excludes major event days, when its recorded cause is customer equipment, or when its recorded cause is planned maintenance or a public safety shutoff, both of which are announced in advance. No sustained-outage credit is posted for a record that does not qualify.
4. **Excess hours.** The excess hours are the qualifying duration less the minimum duration.
5. **Full increments.** The number of full increments is the excess hours divided by the schedule's outage credit increment hours, rounded down to a whole number.
6. **Credit.** The sustained-outage credit is the schedule's outage credit base amount plus the schedule's outage credit increment amount for each full increment, and that sum is then limited to the schedule's outage credit cap: the credit is the lower of the sum and the cap.
7. **Rounding.** No intermediate figure is rounded; only the final credit is rounded to the cent.

The schedule figures named above are those of the schedule the agreement is billed on.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

Hypothetical schedule values: minimum outage credit duration 20 hours, base amount $40.00, increment amount $20.00, increment hours 8, cap $120.00, major event days excluded. Each hypothetical record has a recorded cause other than customer equipment, planned maintenance or a public safety shutoff unless stated.

| Hypothetical record | Qualifies | Excess hours | Full increments | Base plus increments | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 45.5 hours | yes | 25.5 | 3 (25.5 divided by 8 is 3.1875) | $40.00 plus 3 times $20.00, $100.00 | $100.00 |
| 70.0 hours | yes | 50.0 | 6 (6.25 rounded down) | $160.00 | $120.00 (limited to the cap) |
| 20.0 hours | yes, at the minimum | 0 | 0 | $40.00 | $40.00 |
| 19.9 hours | no | not reached | none | none | no credit |
| 30.0 hours, began on a major event day | no | not reached | none | none | no credit |
| 30.0 hours, cause customer equipment | no | not reached | none | none | no credit |

title: Care Desk Tool Reference Card — Posting a Sustained-Outage Credit on an Electric Service Agreement
content:
**Electric Service Agreement — sustained-outage credit posting.**

**Posting rule.** A sustained-outage credit is posted to the agreement, without waiting for the customer to ask, for the most recent outage record at its service address once that record qualifies.

| Point | Under the posting rule |
|---|---|
| Who initiates | The company posts the credit; no request from the customer is needed. |
| Record compensated | The most recent outage record at the agreement's service address. |
| When | Once that record qualifies. |
| Where it is booked | The Electric Service Agreement whose service address had the outage. |

## Tool: `grant_sustained_outage_credit_20084a33`

**Invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `grant_sustained_outage_credit_20084a33` and then calls it. One call books exactly one sustained-outage credit for the outage record named.

**Effect.** The credit is booked on the agreement as a new sustained-outage credit dated today, tied to the outage record it compensates, and the agreement's balance owed falls by the credited amount. The customer sees the credit on the account right away and on the next bill.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the electric service agreement whose service address had the outage, as returned by the service agreement lookup. | Identifier |
| `outage_event_id` | The reference number of the outage record being compensated, as returned by the outage record lookup for that agreement. | Identifier |
| `amount` | The credit in US dollars. | A positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); a value with more decimals is rounded half-up to the cent when it is booked. |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence stating the new credit reference number (an opaque id beginning "soc_"), the outage reference number, the credited amount in USD with 2 decimal places, the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the agreement's new balance owed in USD with 2 decimal places. Receiving this sentence means the credit is posted.

title: Sustained Outage Credit Terms for Electric Service Agreement Customers
content:
Under the **Electric Service Agreement**, Lakeshore Power & Light Company grants sustained-outage credits on the terms below. "Outage record" means the company's record of an interruption at the customer's service address.

## Terms no longer in force
- The term under which a sustained-outage credit was granted on the customer's request for an outage record at the service address lasting at least the schedule's minimum qualifying duration is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.
- The term that set the credit as the schedule's base credit plus a schedule increment for each full increment of duration beyond the minimum, up to the schedule's cap, is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

## Terms in force
**Exclusions.** No credit is granted:
- for an outage on a major event day, when the schedule excludes major event days from outage credits;
- for a planned maintenance outage or a public safety shutoff outage announced in advance;
- for an outage caused by customer equipment.

**Claim window.** The credit must be requested no later than the claim window after the restoration of service after the outage. The window is the schedule's claim window in calendar days, counted starting the day after the restoration date, and a request on the last day is accepted. The restoration date is the one on the outage record.

Hypothetical case (restoration on 4 June; a 30-day window chosen only for illustration): day one of the window is 5 June and the last day is 4 July. A request on 4 July is within the window; a request on 5 July is outside it.

**One credit per code.** Each outage record earns at most one credit of each credit code; a second sustained-outage credit is never granted for an outage record that already carries one.

**Governing schedule.** The schedule in effect on the outage start date governs, even when the agreement has since moved to another schedule.

**Chronic-outage credit.** A chronic-outage credit is decided separately and stacks with this credit, so one outage record may carry both a sustained-outage credit and a chronic-outage credit.

title: Schedules RT, REV and GST: Time-of-Use Bill Protection Worked Examples
content:
Billing analyst sheet for the **Electric Service Agreement**: bill protection on the time-of-use schedules (Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service, Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service, Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service).

## Rule
A customer who joins Schedule RT, REV or GST receives bill protection for the schedule's bill protection period, in months, starting on the date that schedule took effect on the agreement. After the last bill of the protection period, the energy charges of every regular bill in the period are recomputed under the base flat schedule using the same kWh, and when the total actually billed exceeds the recomputed total, the difference is credited once as a time-of-use bill protection billing credit whose source reference is the agreement itself. No credit is due when the time-of-use total is equal or lower. Bill protection is granted once per service agreement; it ends early without any credit when the customer leaves the time-of-use schedule before the period ends.

| Time-of-use schedule joined | Base flat schedule used for the recomputation |
|---|---|
| Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service | Schedule RS Residential Standard Service |
| Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service | Schedule RS Residential Standard Service |
| Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service | Schedule GS Small General Service |

## Worked examples (all figures hypothetical)
**Example A, Schedule REV.** Energy charges actually billed on the regular bills of the period total 1,184.60 USD. The same kWh priced under Schedule RS total 1,139.25 USD. The billed total exceeds the recomputed total by 1,184.60 less 1,139.25, that is 45.35 USD, credited once after the last bill of the period.

**Example B, Schedule GST.** Billed total 2,310.00 USD; recomputed under Schedule GS 2,310.00 USD. The totals are equal, so no credit is due. The same holds for any billed total below the recomputed total.

**Example C, Schedule RT.** The customer leaves Schedule RT before the protection period ends. Protection ends early and no credit is posted, whatever the two totals would have shown.

**Example D.** The agreement already carries a time-of-use bill protection credit. Protection is granted once per service agreement, so no second credit is posted on it.

title: Training Note: Transferred Balances and Late-Payment History in the Electric Service Agreement Past-Due Balance
content:
**Electric Service Agreement.** When a customer pays toward the past-due minimum for a written disconnection notice, a balance transferred from a closed agreement (a balance-transfer debit on the agreement) counts toward the past-due balance according to the late payment charges posted on the agreement in the 24 calendar months before the payment:

- **two or more late payment charges** — the transferred balance counts in full;
- **exactly one late payment charge** — it counts at half (0.5) of its amount, with any fraction of a cent dropped;
- **no late payment charge** — it does not count at all.

The counted part of the transferred balance is part of the past-due balance, alongside the agreement's bills and other charges, before any payments and credits are subtracted from it and before the allowance under the notice minimum is subtracted.

## Questions answered

**Which late payment charges are counted?** Those posted on the same agreement the payment is for. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date; the posting here is the payment.

**What does "fraction of a cent dropped" mean in figures?** A hypothetical transferred balance of USD 75.25 counts as USD 37.62 at half: half is 37.625, and the part below the cent is dropped, not rounded up.

**And the window edge?** Hypothetical: payment on 20 June. A late payment charge dated 20 June two years earlier is exactly 24 whole calendar months before and is not counted; one dated 21 June two years earlier is counted.

**Worked comparison (hypothetical USD 75.25 transferred):** two late payment charges, 75.25 counts; one, 37.62 counts; none, 0.00 counts.

title: Notice Surcharge on Late Payment Charges for Electric Service Agreements with Repeated Disconnection Notices
content:
Credit & Collections applies a notice surcharge to the late payment charge on an Electric Service Agreement whose history shows repeated written disconnection notices.

## Provision

A notice surcharge is added to the late payment charge after the minimum is applied: 3.00 dollars when three or more written disconnection notices were served on the agreement in the 12 calendar months before this charge, 1.50 dollars when exactly two were, and nothing when one or none was. The late payment charge with the surcharge added is stated rounded to the cent. The surcharge attaches to a late payment charge that arises; where no part of the bill is unpaid, no late payment charge arises and there is nothing to add it to.

Only written disconnection notices count; final notices delivered by phone call or door hanger are not written notices. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date.

## Surcharge scale

| Written disconnection notices served on the agreement in the 12 calendar months before the charge | Notice surcharge |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 3.00 USD |
| exactly 2 | 1.50 USD |
| 1 or none | nothing |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

| Late payment charge after the minimum | Written notices in the 12 months | Surcharge | Late payment charge posted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.74 | 1 | nothing | 2.74 |
| 2.74 | 2 | 1.50 | 4.24 |
| 1.00 (the minimum) | 3 | 3.00 | 4.00 |
| 5.12 | 4 | 3.00 | 8.12 |

In the third row the minimum has already been applied, and the surcharge of 3.00 is added to that minimum.
